description:
Rank several candidate strategies by how likely each is to trade at all, before spending backtests on them. Give it one asset and up to 99 candidates, each {entry: [...], exit: [...]} with signals from the library -- the roles come from the library, so do not pass signal_type. IT PREDICTS WHETHER A STRATEGY WILL PLACE TRADES, AND NOTHING ABOUT WHETHER IT WILL MAKE MONEY: only a backtest answers that. Use it to choose which of many candidates to backtest first, never as a verdict on a single strategy -- a probability on its own says little, and the ranking is the answer. A HIGH score is real support for spending a backtest. A LOW score is weak evidence and is NOT a finding that the strategy will not trade: measured against runs that did trade, a 0.5 cutoff recovers under half of them. Never tell someone their strategy will not trade because this scored it low; back it and find out.

[Access: pay 0.02 USDC via x402 (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header) OR authenticate with an API key. An x402-capable client will auto-pay; API-key clients pay nothing per call.]
